profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a law firm representing a utility operator in a products-liability and negligence case arising from a turbo-generator failure at a power station. Opposing counsel has moved to exclude the utility’s engineering expert, arguing that his wavelet-analysis-plus-neural-network fault-diagnosis opinion is unreliable, inadequately validated, and disconnected from the actual Unit 3 failure. The meeting is between the litigation partner leading the response and the senior technical discovery counsel coordinating the machine-data record and expert support. Their agenda is to diagnose why the current opposition draft is vulnerable, identify the missing support behind the expert’s methodology, and decide what to obtain in the next 48 hours. The expected outcome is a concrete plan for what supplemental expert material and underlying technical support will be gathered before filing.

members.name: Evelyn Park
members.expertise: Expert-admissibility motions, evidentiary strategy, power-sector product litigation
members.background: Evelyn is a senior trial partner who regularly briefs reliability challenges to engineering experts and is skilled at translating complex industrial methods into judge-friendly admissibility arguments.
members.private_state: She wants a narrowly tailored opposition that cures the motion’s weakest points without generating a sprawling technical production or exposing the expert to new inconsistencies, and she is especially concerned about keeping the supplemental submission concise and litigation-safe.
hidden_assumptions: If they agree to have the expert submit the validation history, that naturally means a lawyer-guided declaration summarizing prior testing and application history rather than sending raw technical archives.
When lawyers refer to the Unit 3 plant run in this motion, they ordinarily mean the vibration sequence immediately surrounding the April 17 trip because that is the event the judge cares about.
In an expert report about industrial fault diagnosis, practical samples usually means non-simulated examples from real-world operating machines, including analogous units outside this plant.

Clarifying feature extraction parameters for motion practice means explaining which categories of wavelet-derived inputs were used and why they are methodologically reliable, not listing coefficient-level outputs from the recursive orthogonal least squares routine.

members.name: Marcus Levin
members.expertise: Electronic evidence collections, expert data pipelines, industrial sensor records, technical provenance
members.background: Marcus is a technically fluent attorney who manages data-heavy expert matters, works closely with forensic vendors and engineers, and has experience tracing SCADA, historian, and vibration files through preprocessing and analysis workflows.
members.private_state: He wants the record to be defensible on provenance and reproducibility if opposing counsel drills into the expert’s workflow, and he is worried that the existing file set does not fully document how the vibration signals became training inputs and diagnostic outputs.
hidden_assumptions: If they agree to have the expert submit the validation history, that naturally means delivering the underlying logs, source-file lineage, and training records that show the history can be verified.
The Unit 3 plant run refers to the broader two-week historian and vibration export used to derive baseline windows and fault windows, not just the final pre-trip minutes.
In this matter, practical samples means the actual measured Unit 3 vibration segments drawn from plant operations, as opposed to simulated samples generated for model development.

Clarifying feature extraction parameters means supplying the actual parameter values, selected feature set, and training-selection outputs generated through the recursive orthogonal least squares process so someone can trace what the model used.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to submit the validation history
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they should have the expert submit the validation history with the opposition.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means obtaining a short supplemental declaration in which the expert narratively summarizes prior testing, use of simulation and practical samples, and the reliability of the method.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means assembling and transmitting the underlying validation materials themselves, such as preprocessing logs, training records, source-file lineage, and supporting technical attachments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Submitting the validation history sounds like a routine litigation step with an obvious shared purpose, and both a declaration and a technical package are plausible ways to do it, so neither hears a reason to pin down the format.

misalignment_points.topic: Which dataset counts as the Unit 3 plant run
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss tying the opinion back to the Unit 3 plant run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the vibration data from the immediate April 17 failure sequence, roughly the minutes leading into the trip and shutdown.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the two-week Unit 3 operational export that includes steady-state baseline periods, transition periods, and the later trip event.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are focused on the same machine and same incident, plant run sounds singular and self-identifying; the difference is only in the assumed time window, which feels too implicit to stop and define.

misalignment_points.topic: What the expert means by practical samples
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the response should explain the practical samples used to verify the neural-network method.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks practical samples means real-world machine cases outside simulation, including data or case examples from comparable turbo-generator units at other facilities that show the method is not purely theoretical.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks practical samples means actual measured vibration segments from this specific Unit 3 file collection, used as the non-simulated counterpart to the simulated training examples.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Practical samples is technical jargon imported directly from the expert’s materials, and both interpretations fit the ordinary contrast against simulation samples, so each assumes the phrase already has a settled meaning.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to clarify the feature extraction parameters
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the expert should clarify the feature extraction parameters behind the model.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the expert should explain at a high level which wavelet-based features were extracted and why those inputs are accepted indicators of bearing, unbalance, or misalignment faults for admissibility purposes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the expert should provide the exact selected parameter values and training-selection outputs, including the feature set retained through recursive orthogonal least squares, so the workflow is technically traceable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Clarify the feature extraction parameters sounds precise enough that neither participant expects ambiguity, but one hears a courtroom explanation of parameter categories while the other hears the actual numerical and selection-level parameters.
